transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-23 14:00 PT - Duration 38 minutes. Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (NovaHealth Head of ML), Raj Patel (NovaHealth Platform Eng), Maya Chen (NovaHealth SRE).

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency/throughput) comparing Redwood runs vs baseline provider. Discussed tuning done (batching, KV cache warmup, quantization profile), observed 95th/99th percentile latency differences, some outliers due to cold-starts and network egress. Agreed next steps: share raw logs, run dedicated config 99th-pctl tests, share SOC II + KMS docs, schedule follow-up.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, do we have the right list? Sara, Raj, Maya from NovaHealth, and Priya and I from Redwood, yes?
[00:06] Sara: yep this is Sara, good to go.
[00:08] Raj: Raj here.
[00:10] Maya: Maya, all set.
[00:12] Alex: cool, quick agenda - run through the benchmark slides i shared, call out the 95/99 pctl latency, look at throughput at target qps, note any configuration changes since last week, and agree next steps. priya will jump in on the tuning bits.
[00:28] Priya: hey team, i'll start with the numbers - two test suites run: steady-state throughput at 200 qps and burst at 500 qps for 30 minutes. baseline provider is the one you had been running, labelled OtherProviderX in the sheet. we ran Redwood hosted config and a dedicated pool config (4 gpus, mixed quant).
[00:45] Priya: highlights: median latency comparable ~60-70ms per token for both, but at 95th and 99th we see Redwood dedicated is lower - 95th at ~210ms vs baseline 320ms, 99th at ~420ms vs baseline 740ms. now these are per-token-ish numbers, end-to-end generation for your 512 token prompt is what you care about, so the end-to-end 99th was roughly 3.6s on Redwood dedicated vs ~6.1s on baseline in our runs.
[01:12] Sara: okay that's promising, our main concern is tail latency for synchronous API calls on the clinician UI. We need 99th under 5s for the 512 token case. looks like dedicated config meets that?
[01:20] Priya: yes in tuned dedicated runs we hit ~3.6s 99th. hosted runs on Redwood were closer to 4.8s 99th - still under 5s but more variable.
[01:28] Raj: can you remind us what caused the big delta at 99th - is that network, kv cache, or batching behavior?
[01:34] Priya: good question. primary contributors were cold KV cache misses at the start of the test, and a few scheduling pauses during burst windows. we also saw some significant network egress spikes in the baseline provider runs - their multi-tenant noisy neighbor patterns showed up. for our dedicated pool we have more consistent kernel selection and pinned GPUs so that reduced jitter.
[01:50] Maya: the term KV cash was in the doc, is that the key-value cache? you mean KV cache? we saw some warmup weirdness.
[01:55] Priya: yes sorry, KV cache - and we did a warmup script this week to prime prefixes which reduced tail by ~18% in our measurements.
[02:05] Alex: we also applied a slightly more aggressive quantization profile on the dedicated runs (int8-mixed) which reduced GPU utilization and improved throughput per card. that had minor quality delta but you told us quality tolerances are wide for the summarization path.
[02:22] Sara: quality is fine in spot checks, thanks. any changes to memory/kv cache footprint that would impact your SRE?
[02:28] Maya: we watch memory footprints closely. the mixed int8 path decreased memory but increased CPU postprocessing a bit - that's ok for us as long as p95/p99 stays stable.
[02:36] Priya: noted. we can provide the per-task memory breakdown.
[02:40] [03:00] Priya: moving to throughput - at 200 qps steady-state both Redwood and baseline handled it fine, baseline had slightly higher peak throughput in short bursts but at cost of much higher tail latency. at sustained 500 qps burst, Redwood dedicated maintained 480-510 qps with far fewer retries; baseline had retries and queue spikes causing higher end-to-end slowing.
[03:25] Raj: retries - were those application level (client retries) or infra (provider throttling)?
[03:29] Priya: infra level mostly, we saw provider-side rate limiting kick in, causing backoff cascades. Redwood's dedicated pool maintained headroom.
[03:36] Sara: any noted differences in tokenization or model variants used? i think baseline was running v2.1 while you used 2.0-compat?
[03:44] Priya: yes the baseline was a v2.1 variant which has slightly different decode behavior. for apples-to-apples we ran Redwood on a 2.1-compatible variant and also tried a 2.0-profiled run - numbers i shared are from the 2.1-compatible. small diffs but not the driver of the tail.
[03:58] Alex: quick note on cost: per-token cost for dedicated during these runs was materially lower than baseline once you amortize reserved capacity for your expected qps; i put a cost model in the sheet.
[04:10] Raj: can you re-share the cost model with assumptions broken out? like reserved GPU hourly, data egress, and batching assumptions?
[04:15] Alex: yes will resend with line items.
[04:18] [05:00] Maya: we ran some internal tests too and saw occasional 7-8s spikes on Redwood hosted last week, is that consistent with what you saw?
[05:07] Priya: those spikes are likely cold-starts on hosted and occasional placement events; hosted is slightly more variable - that is why dedicated is recommended when you need stable 99th pctl. we can tune container warmup and prefix caching to mitigate, but the elimination is not perfect in multi-tenant hosted.
[05:26] Sara: for the pilot we probably want to start with hosted then move to dedicated before cutover to prod, timeline about 4-6 weeks. any blockers for that approach?
[05:35] Alex: that's a standard approach, no blockers from Redwood side. we can start with hosted for integration and run production-ish traffic in a canary, then flip to dedicated when SLOs are validated.
[05:45] Raj: networking question - for dedicated pool will we need VPC peering or can you support private link?
[05:50] Priya: we support both VPC peering and private link. for the dedicated we recommend VPC peering for lower latency. we'll share IP ranges and associated firewall rules.
[05:59] Raj: any compliance docs for SOC - we need SOC two and KMS details for our security review.
[06:05] Alex: yes we'll send SOC II, ISO, and our KMS integration docs. I'll include the redwood-private deployment notes too in case you decide to go VPC/on-prem.
[06:15] [06:30] Priya: quick run-through of a couple of anomaly traces - i uploaded three trace links in the sheet: trace A shows a KV miss at t0 which adds ~180ms; trace B is a scheduling pause due to a node rebalancing event during the baseline run; trace C is network egress jitter from their multi-tenant host. links: (sheet row links) - see "benchmark raw logs" link in the deck.
[06:54] Maya: those links were useful, i can see the KV warmup difference. for the warmup, what script did you run? we want to run an equivalent pre-warm in our infra.
[07:02] Priya: it's a simple prefix prime script - replay top 200 prefixes from your dev corpus over five minutes, then run a short synthetic load. i'll drop the script in the spreadsheet. note you should run it before big bursts.
[07:18] Sara: question on model fallback - if dedicated capacity is saturated, do you have automatic fallback to hosted or to a smaller model?
[07:25] Alex: yes smart routing supports fallback policies - you can route to a lower-cost model variant or to hosted as a fallback. we can set a canary/burst policy so critical routes prefer dedicated but spillover goes to hosted.
[07:36] Raj: what's the RPC timeout recommended for synchronous calls? we have a 10s client timeout now - will that be enough?
[07:42] Priya: for 512-token 99th targets below 5s, 10s is fine but I'd recommend 12s for safety during transitional runs. if you do long-context or higher token counts, bump accordingly.
[07:53] [08:00] Alex: ok let's capture open items: we'll send raw logs and updated sheet; priya will run the 99th pctl dedicated tests; raj will confirm network windows; sara will finalize success criteria. scheduled follow-up next week.
[08:12] Sara: sounds good. two quick clarifications - are there any model quality regressions with int8 quant you observed (hallucination/formatting)?
[08:20] Priya: minimal; we ran automated evals on your prompt set and human spot checks - no systematic regressions. we'll include the eval outputs in the sheet.
[08:30] Raj: also can you include a breakdown of egress costs in the cost model? that's a big driver for us.
[08:34] Alex: will do.
[08:36] Maya: one more SRE note - please call out any changes to TLS termination or certificate chains for VPC peering.
[08:42] Alex: noted, will include in the network appendix.
[08:45] [09:00] Quick recap and next steps.
[09:05] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll get the benchmark artifacts over by Thursday, and priya will post tuned-run results by Monday. follow-up on 2026-06-30 10am PT.
[09:15] Sara: thanks, bye.
[09:18] Raj: bye.
[09:20] Maya: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript has minor transcription noise and occasional speaker label drift. References: "benchmark raw logs" (sheet link), SOC II & KMS docs (to be shared), warmup script (to be attached in spreadsheet).
